questions.question: Which nutrient provides a significant amount of energy during lower- intensity, long-duration exercise? a). Fat b). Protein c). Vitamin C d). Calcium / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• During-exercise Phase
  • Dos
  • • Drink fluids regularly according to thirst, sweat rate and environmental conditions.
  • • Use carbohydrate-containing sports drinks or foods during prolonged endurance exercise when
  • appropriate.
  • • Replace electrolytes, particularly sodium, during prolonged exercise with substantial sweat
  • losses.
  • • Follow an individualized hydration and fueling plan practised during training.
  • • Monitor fatigue, thirst and other signs of dehydration.
  • Don'ts
  • • Do not ignore thirst or significant fluid losses.
  • • Avoid excessive fluid intake, which may cause exercise-associated hyponatremia.
  • • Do not consume large quantities of food that may cause gastrointestinal discomfort.
  • • Avoid experimenting with new sports drinks or supplements during competition.
  • • Do not rely on energy drinks as a substitute for proper hydration and nutrition.

  • per meal in healthy adults, supporting muscle growth and repair.

questions.question: Explain pre-exercise, during-exercise and post-exercise hydration strategies for endurance athletes? / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain pre -exercise, during -exercise and post -exercise hydration strategies for endurance
  • athletes.
  • Pre-exercise hydration
  • • Athletes should begin exercise in a well -hydrated state to prevent early dehydration and
  • maintain performance.
  • • They should drink approximately 5 –7 mL of fluid per kilogram of body weight about 4 hours
  • before exercise.
  • • If urine output is low or urine remains dark, an additional 3 –5 mL/kg about 2 hours before
  • exercise may be consumed.
  • • Water is generally sufficient for shorter activities, while electrolyte -containing drinks may be
  • useful in hot conditions or during prolonged endurance events.
  • • Athletes should avoid excessive fluid intake immediately before exercise to prevent stomach
  • discomfort and frequent urination.

questions.question: As a coach, design a checklist of "dos and don'ts" for athletes to avoid the common nutritional mistakes discussed in this unit, covering pre- exercise, during-exercise, and post-exercise phases. / [CO5] [15x2 = 30]
questions.solution_html:
• As a coach, design a checklist of “dos and don'ts” for athletes to avoid common nutritional
  • mistakes during pre-exercise, during-exercise and post-exercise phases.
  • . Pre-exercise Phase
  • Dos
  • • Eat a balanced meal rich in carbohydrates 2–4 hours before exercise to provide sufficient
  • energy.
  • • Include moderate amounts of protein to support muscle function.
  • • Drink adequate fluids before exercise to begin the session well hydrated.
  • • Choose familiar, easily digestible foods to prevent stomach discomfort.
  • • Adjust meal timing and portion sizes according to exercise intensity and duration.
  • Don'ts
  • • Do not exercise on an empty stomach if it causes weakness or poor performance.
